clue.text: Studying the form of mounts

parts.note: mounts here are mountains, not horses or picture frames, so the clue describes the science of mapping the shape of high ground

explanation.surface: Someone examines the shape of horses or stands for display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mounts' suggests horses or frames for pictures; here it is the poetic word for mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: The term names the branch of physical geography that describes the relief and elevation of mountains.

clue.text: Suggestion's inappropriate, meeting hesitation

definitions.note: read as 'suggestion is', the 's linking the definition to the wordplay

parts.note: off can mean unsuitable or out of order, as in 'that remark was a bit off'
er is the sound a speaker makes while hesitating

explanation.surface: A proposal is judged unsuitable when it is delivered with hesitation.
explanation.definitionFit: A proposal or bid put forward for acceptance is a suggestion of terms.

clue.text: It restricts movements of rower or limits a rugby forward

indicators.note: to limit is to bound, so the word or forms the boundary on either side of the following a

parts.note: taken as written
a lock is a second-row forward in a rugby scrum

explanation.surface: A device holds back a rower, or some rule constrains a rugby player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rower' looks like fodder for the first piece but belongs to the definition; 'limits' is a verb, with OR enclosing A.
explanation.definitionFit: The fitting on a boat's gunwale holds the oar in place so the rower's stroke pivots on it.

clue.text: Sort of music from harp disco oddly used

indicators.note: letters used in an odd or unusual way are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Some style of music is produced by playing a harp at a disco in a strange way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' might suggest taking odd letters, but with 'used' it signals that HARP and DISCO are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Music described as free, emotional and in the style of a rhapsody is of this sort.

clue.text: Changing shape involves skin mostly being constrained to fit

indicators.note: to involve is to contain within, so the first piece wraps around the second

parts.note: protean means able to change form, after the sea god Proteus

indicators.note: most of the word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: a crust is a hard outer skin, as on bread

explanation.surface: Something altering its form takes in a skin while being forced into a fixed size.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Changing shape' looks like an anagram signal; it is the definition of a single word, which then takes in the trimmed skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Procrustes in Greek myth stretched or lopped his guests to fit his bed, so the adjective means forcing conformity ruthlessly.

clue.text: Agreement with conclusions of jury — and vice versa

indicators.note: the conclusions of words are their final letters, taken here from jury, vice and versa

explanation.surface: A jury reaches agreement, and the reverse holds too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vice versa' looks like an instruction to reverse something; its two words simply supply their last letters along with jury's.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic or parliamentary word for yes, used to signal assent in a vote.

clue.text: Muslim city in grip of doctrine

indicators.note: held in the grip of something means enclosed by it, so the city sits inside the doctrine

parts.note: an ism is any distinctive doctrine or system of belief
LA is Los Angeles, the city crosswords most often abbreviate

explanation.surface: A Muslim city is held fast by a religious teaching.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is used loosely: the faith of Muslims, standing for 'Muslim' as a noun for the religion.
explanation.definitionFit: The religion practised by Muslims, so the one word stands for its followers' faith.

clue.text: Man's name — it is visible in the first clue

annotationWithheld.why: Man's name — it is visible in the first clue: no parse found for ISAAC; 'visible in the first clue' points to an unidentified hidden or referential device
annotationWithheld.clue: Man's name — it is visible in the first clue

clue.text: Rock singer's traditional stuff sure to be forgotten in more relaxed times

definitions.note: read as 'rock singer is', the 's linking definition to wordplay

parts.note: lore is the body of traditional knowledge passed down

indicators.note: the word sure is to be dropped from within the following piece

parts.note: leisure is time spent more relaxed, free from work
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rock musician's old-fashioned material is certain to be overlooked when life gets easier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock singer' suggests a pop star; it is the siren of the Rhine who sat on a rock and lured boatmen. LEISURE loses SURE to leave LEI.
explanation.definitionFit: In German legend a siren on a cliff above the Rhine sang sailors to their doom.

clue.text: Notes from me, and doctor hurried to lawyer

parts.note: taken as written
MO is a medical officer, an army doctor
ran means moved quickly
DA is a district attorney, an American prosecuting lawyer

explanation.surface: Messages sent from me, while a doctor rushed off to see an attorney.
explanation.walkthrough: 'And' here is a link word, not part of an anagram: the pieces sit side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Formal written memos are notes kept as reminders or for circulation.

clue.text: Medley including nothing after long jazz piece

indicators.note: the round letter comes after the earlier pieces in the answer

parts.note: far means a long way, distant
a rag is a piece of ragtime music
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A musical medley contains a silent pause following a lengthy jazz number.
explanation.definitionFit: A confused mixture or hotchpotch of things is a jumble, the same as a medley.

clue.text: A worry with computer memory — it's rearranged characters

parts.note: to nag is to worry or pester someone
RAM is random-access memory in a computer

explanation.surface: A concern about a computer's memory is just letters in the wrong order.
explanation.definitionFit: A word or phrase formed by reordering the letters of another is literally reshuffled lettering.

clue.text: Searches throughout earth for solutions

definitions.meaning: a pig or a gardener ... about, digging through soil to look for something
in mathematics the values that satisfy an equation are its ...

explanation.surface: Someone digs all through the soil hunting for answers.
explanation.definitionFit: Rummaging by digging is rooting, and the values solving an equation are its roots.

clue.text: Broadcast of Lucretia Borgia's No. 3 on the network

indicators.note: seed broadcast is scattered widely, so these letters are scattered into a new order
the third letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: A programme about the Borgia daughter's third item is aired on the network.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lucretia Borgia' looks like a single name to treat whole; only her first name is scrambled, and 'No. 3' takes one letter from the surname.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes something arranged like a net, a mesh of crossing lines.

clue.text: A crowded reign?

parts.note: a rule shared by several people is crowded compared with one monarch on the throne, here a government by three

explanation.surface: A monarch's rule seems overpopulated.
explanation.definitionFit: Rome's ruling trio, such as Caesar, Pompey and Crassus, shared power among three men.

clue.text: I Kings appears to be provocative

parts.note: the numeral one is written as the Roman I
R (rex) and K are both abbreviations for king, giving two kings

explanation.surface: A book of the Bible seems designed to stir people up.
explanation.walkthrough: '1 Kings' looks like a book of the Old Testament; it is I followed by two king abbreviations. The definition is the verb 'to be provocative', to annoy.
explanation.definitionFit: To annoy or irritate someone is to provoke them.

clue.text: Trying it out, injecting Ecstasy? So much for upright attitude!

indicators.note: something injected is put inside, so the drug letter goes into the rearranged letters
out signals the letters are disordered or set out afresh

parts.note: E is the street abbreviation for the drug Ecstasy

explanation.surface: Someone experimenting with drugs abandons any moral standards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges TRYING IT and 'injecting' puts E into the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Honesty and firm moral principle make up a person's upright character.

clue.text: Want a little money once for first part of repayment

indicators.note: the new letter takes the place of the opening letter of the next piece

parts.note: restitution is compensation or repayment for a loss
D was the abbreviation for a penny in pre-decimal British money

explanation.surface: Someone needs a small coin to make the first instalment of a repayment.
explanation.walkthrough: Old British pennies were written d (from Latin denarius); D replaces the R of RESTITUTION.
explanation.definitionFit: Severe poverty is being in want, lacking the basic necessities.

clue.text: Bun without topping? Without topping and overlooked

indicators.note: a word without its topping loses its first letter

parts.note: without means not having
iced means covered with icing, a cake topping

explanation.surface: A plain bun with no glaze passes by without anyone paying attention.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated phrase works two ways: first it beheads BUN, then it is read literally as NOT ICED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something not spotted or noticed has been missed by everyone.

clue.text: Eager consumer's payment mostly pinched by crooked merchant

definitions.note: read as 'eager consumer is', the 's linking to wordplay

indicators.note: pinched means gripped, so the payment piece is held inside the other
crooked means bent out of shape, so the letters are rearranged
most of the word, losing its last letter

parts.note: rent is a regular payment for property

explanation.surface: A keen customer's payment has largely been stolen by a dishonest trader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pinched' suggests stealing; here it means gripped, as in held between finger and thumb.
explanation.definitionFit: A hearty eater, one who sets to with gusto at the table, is an enthusiastic consumer of food.

clue.text: Preference for flower? It is found in a tree

indicators.note: found in means located inside, so the phrase goes within the tree

parts.note: an elm is a familiar tree
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gardener's love of blooms is located in a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is not a bloom but the best of a group, as in 'the flower of youth'.
explanation.definitionFit: Favouring an elite, the choicest few, is a preference for society's finest.

clue.text: What's visible from position on board (even though docked)?

indicators.note: docked means cut short at the tail, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a seat is a position on a board of directors

explanation.surface: A view from a ship's deck, even when the ship is moored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' suggests a ship and 'docked' a harbour; here a board seat is shortened.
explanation.definitionFit: Water stretching to the horizon is what a passenger looks out on from a deck.

clue.text: I'm consumed by' terrible lust, one providing incentives

indicators.note: consumed means swallowed up, so the first word goes inside the other
terrible signals the letters are mangled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written without the apostrophe
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A person admits being eaten up by awful desire, which spurs them on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One providing incentives' reads as a single person; 'one' gives a letter and the plural answer is the things that provide them.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that spur action or response, such as incentives, are the plural of stimulus.

clue.text: These are translatable as "sliding"

indicators.note: something translatable can be turned into another form, so these letters can be reworked

explanation.surface: Some musical terms might be rendered in English as gliding.
explanation.walkthrough: AS and SLIDING are rearranged; the whole clue also describes the answer, glides in music.
explanation.definitionFit: In music, rapid slides up or down a scale are what this Italianate plural names.

clue.text: Demonstrated a fabric

definitions.meaning: protesters ..., occupying a place as a demonstration
a smooth glossy cloth woven from silk

explanation.surface: A protest was staged over some cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the first sense as two words, SAT IN, as in a protest sit-in.
explanation.definitionFit: A glossy woven cloth, and the phrase for protesters occupying a place.

clue.text: Uninspiring religious observance at front of temple

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a rite is a religious ceremony

explanation.surface: A dull ceremony is held at the entrance to a temple.
explanation.definitionFit: Hackneyed and stale, an overused remark lacks any originality.

clue.text: Praise former work after one's dismissal

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: a dismissal sends something away, so the letter is removed

parts.note: toil is hard work
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone lauds an old job after being fired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' is a link word here, not an order indicator; the deletion is signalled by 'dismissal' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: To laud something highly is to commend it with enthusiasm.

clue.text: Silly clipped way of speaking, a nervous response

indicators.note: clipped means trimmed short, so the last letter goes

parts.note: an idiom is a characteristic manner of expression
a tic is an involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: Someone's terse speech comes with a jittery twitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clipped way of speaking' wants to be a curt manner; it is IDIOM cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: Foolish, stupid behaviour is daft or senseless.

clue.text: It could be either end of whippet

definitions.text: It could be either end of whippet

parts.words: It could be either end of whippet
parts.note: split the dog's name into whip and pet: a whip can be a ...-o'-nine-tails and a pet is often a feline, so both halves give the same word

explanation.surface: Something describes either the head or tail of a racing dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'End' suggests letters; it means each half of the split word.
explanation.definitionFit: A feline pet, and the short name of a nine-tailed whip.

clue.text: A Conservative nobleman's relation

parts.note: a count is a European nobleman

explanation.surface: A Tory aristocrat has a relative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relation' looks like a family member; it means a telling or report.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrative report or story is a relation of events.

clue.text: Farmers overlooking nothing in the country

indicators.note: overlooking means ignoring, so the letter is left out

parts.note: yeomen were small freeholding farmers
O looks like zero

explanation.surface: Agricultural workers fail to notice anything in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The country' looks like rural land; it is a nation in the Arabian peninsula.
explanation.definitionFit: A nation on the southern tip of the Arabian peninsula.

clue.text: Teacher's first instruction to economics student may be routine work

indicators.note: first means the opening letter of the word

parts.note: 'read Mill' tells a student to study John Stuart Mill, the political economist

explanation.surface: A tutor's opening advice to an economics undergraduate may be dull drudgery.
explanation.walkthrough: John Stuart Mill was a 19th-century British economist and philosopher.
explanation.definitionFit: Monotonous, unvarying labour is like walking on a moving belt that goes nowhere.
